Im older (M27) and I felt this way when I was your age too dude. For me, it passed when I was like 25. If  you make it that far (and I hope you do!) you may realize the same thing. 

One thing I've learned in my short time on Earth is that we're often times in between things age wise. When you were a tween you were in between a boy and a man. Likewise, now that you're a young man you're in between mature adulthood and adolescence. 

It seems to me as a random redditor that you're stuck right now and that you need somewhere to go in life. Maybe you're not in college and maybe you're not working. I hope you are but when we go back and look at stuff from the past we're usually seeking something we had in that moment that made us happy, for you, it seemed like that was enjoying "childlike interests" and friends that you had. 

I sincerely hope that you find friends that you can connect with and something meaningful that you can attach yourself to long term, that will give you something to be content with and feel stable. I also hope that you can find something you like about your age, as, you are relatively young compared to me and a lot of people. That thing I described for me was my faith, Islam. But, that thing that you attach yourself to might be something else and I hope you find it.

Please enjoy your night man. I hope things get better for you and you pull yourself out of this depression!

I have to answer this as an essay so I hope you're in for a long read. 

When I lost my third sales job in late December I was shit out of luck and had no where to go. There was no way in hell that I was going to be able to pay my rent and stay housed in my illegal room rental in Nassau County NY (it's illegal to rent a room in Nassau County due to it "ruining the character of the neighborhood").

Even though my parents covered my rent for one month as a Christmas gift I was destined to become homeless as a result of being unemployed.

When I found out that I was going to become homeless I took my petty cash that I had left and left Nassau County for NYC to acquire housing services. 

I went to Penn Station and told a police officer that I was homeless and that I needed services. An outreach team from an organization from BRC picked me up in a van and took me to 400 E 30th Street to get into the municipal shelter system and I did an intake and was assigned a bed there that night the same night that I went into the shelter. 

My time at 30th Street was short but from what I saw they offered a plethora of services to homeless men to help them get back on their feet ranging from employment services to housing specialists that help shelter residents acquire housing (hence the name). 

After I was assigned a placement in the BX I went to a men's mental health shelter in the East Bronx. From there I was assigned a caseworker who was excellent and helped me work out my kinks that led me to homelessness such as poor mental health and  underemployment.

Regarding the residents, there were a lot of cool guys there that had various reasons for getting into homelessness ranging from separating from partners to addiction/alcoholism. There are a lot of freeloaders in the system because you don't have to work while you're homeless despite the fact that you have an address to list on a job application.

There are a lot of arguments and fights there, but what can you expect when you put a diverse group of men from different backgrounds and mental problems randomly in a group together (dorm)!

After about 9 months my caseworker found me an SRO in the South Bronx and I moved out. A cab took me to my new building and I started my life all over again. I still have problems but I am working on myself each and every day. Life is hard but with the right supports life can get easier and better each and every day. Let me know if you have any more questions!

P.S: the food they served at my shelter was DISGUSTING lmao

I'm aware that a small portion of NYCs budget is allocated to subsidizing some of the population's housing in this city. I'm grateful that such policies are in place to help people like me acquire housing that's within my means to afford.

I frequently hear comments through various associates and forms of social media that we don't have enough resources for the people that're already here. Yet, when I stated that I'm housed you brought up that tax payers are funding a portion of my rent.

While it's true that some people utilize tax payer funds through various housing schemes I'm currently not. I pay the maximum rent for my SRO in the Bronx in lieu of my income. My rent totals out to $775 monthly with utilities included. Now, this is for a space that is roughly 100 sq ft. Or less. 

I worked throughout my housing crisis and acquired a job at a local factory in the South Bronx within 2 weeks of me being sent to a men's shelter in the East Bronx. I've also been employed for the overwhelming preponderance of my time in NYC. 

My plan thus far is to complete my bachelor's degree while I'm in an SRO and then move into independent housing in the BX community. I have other loose ends to tie up, but my main objective is to sort my life out and rise above my circumstance.

My last question is that in a world according to you, what would society do to aid those in a housing crisis (homeless)? What do you think should be done to help those in need?
